rounds.proof_sketch: K=16 (fixed), k_step starts at 0 and increments by 16. Loop condition is k_step < K, so 0 < 16 is true (first iteration runs), then k_step=16 and 16 < 16 is false (loop exits). The loop executes exactly ONE iteration. The removed __syncthreads() at line 104 only serves to synchronize before the NEXT iteration's shared memory loads, but no next iteration exists.
rounds.survival_reason: The removed __syncthreads() barrier at line 104 is positioned at the end of the k_step loop body. Its purpose is to ensure all threads have finished reading from shared memory (A_tile, B_tile) before any thread begins overwriting those tiles in the next loop iteration. However, with the fixed configuration K=16 and k_step incrementing by 16, the loop body executes exactly once (k_step=0). After the single iteration completes, all threads proceed directly to writing their register accumulators to independent global memory locations. Since there is no second iteration, there is no race condition between reading and writing shared memory across iterations. The __syncthreads() at line 85 still properly synchronizes the shared memory loads before computation begins.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed configuration. K=16 guarantees single loop iteration, making the inter-iteration synchronization barrier semantically unnecessary. Would require K > 16 to trigger a race condition, but shape is fixed.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing removes synchronization barriers inside loops, verify whether the loop actually executes multiple iterations under the test configuration. Single-iteration loops effectively eliminate inter-iteration race conditions, making some __syncthreads() removals undetectable. Consider adding test configurations with larger K values (e.g., K=32) to exercise multi-iteration code paths and expose such synchronization bugs.
